modern: The way of holiness is so straight and plain that the simplest minds can’t go wrong if they keep following it. The worldly wise have many twists and turns, and yet they make terrible blunders and usually miss their goal. Worldly cleverness is a poor, short-sighted thing, and when people choose it as their road, it leads them over dark mountains. Gracious minds know nothing better than to do as the Lord tells them, but this keeps them on the King’s highway, under royal protection.

Dear reader, never for a moment try to get yourself out of a difficulty by a lie or by a questionable act. Keep to the middle of the high road of truth and integrity, and you’ll be following the best possible course. In our lives we must never sail in circles, or dream of dodging. Be just, and fear not. Follow Jesus, and don’t worry about bad consequences. If the worst of troubles could be avoided by doing wrong, we would, in the very attempt, have fallen into an evil worse than any trouble could be. God’s way must be the best way. Follow it even if people think you a fool, and you will be truly wise.
Lord, lead your servants in a plain path, because of their enemies.

notes.note: Travelers, even simple ones, on God’s “way of holiness” ([[Isa.35.8|Isaiah 35:8]]).
Scheming, cunning.
“Before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains” ([[Jer.13.16|Jeremiah 13:16]]).
The main road, kept under the king’s protection ([[Num.20.17|Numbers 20:17]]).
A navigator’s term, used here for going round and round instead of straight.
Dodging and evading; acting deceitfully.
A line from Shakespeare’s *Henry VIII*: “Be just, and fear not.”
“Lead me in a plain path, because of mine enemies” ([[Ps.27.11|Psalm 27:11]]).

modern: This is, in practice, a promise that by careful meditation and by giving our whole mind to our work for the Lord, we’ll make progress everyone can see. We profit from the Word of God not by hurried reading but by deep meditation. We’ll get real profit not by doing a great deal of work sloppily, but by giving our best thought to what we take on. “In all labor there is profit,” but not in fuss and hurry without true heart-energy.

If we divide ourselves between God and money, or between Christ and self, we’ll make no progress. We must give ourselves wholly to holy things, or we’ll be poor traders in heavenly business, and when the books are checked, no profit will show.

Am I a minister? Let me be wholly a minister, and not spend my energy on side issues. What do I have to do with party politics or empty amusements? Am I a Christian? Let me make serving Jesus my occupation, my lifework, my one pursuit. We must be in-and-in with Jesus, and then out-and-out for Jesus, or we’ll make neither progress nor profit, and neither the church nor the world will feel the powerful influence the Lord wants us to have.

notes.note: Progress, growth.
Careless, sloppy.
[[Prov.14.23|Proverbs 14:23]].
Money and wealth, served as a god. “Ye cannot serve God and mammon” ([[Matt.6.24|Matthew 6:24]]).
Counting the stock and checking the books to see what profit has been made.
Closely joined to Jesus, and then wholehearted for him.

modern: Many despise warning and perish. Happy is the one who trembles at the word of the Lord. Josiah did, and he was spared the sight of the disaster the Lord had decided to send on Judah because of her great sins. Do you have this tenderness? Do you practice this humbling of yourself? Then you too will be spared in the evil day. God puts a mark on the people who sigh and cry over the sin of the times. The destroying angel is ordered to keep his sword in its sheath until God’s chosen are sheltered, and they are best known by their godly fear and their trembling at the Word of the Lord. Are the times threatening? Are Roman Catholicism and unbelief advancing with great strides, and do you dread God’s punishment on this polluted nation? Well you might. Yet rest in this promise: “Thou shalt be gathered into thy grave in peace: and thine eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring upon this place.” Better still, the Lord himself may come, and then the days of our mourning will be over.

notes.note: The young king of Judah who tore his clothes and wept when the book of the law was found and read to him ([[2Kgs.22.11|2 Kings 22:11]]).
Tore.
Ruin.
God had a mark set on the foreheads of those “that sigh and that cry for all the abominations” of Jerusalem, and they were spared ([[Ezek.9.4|Ezekiel 9:4]]).
Like the angels told to hurt nothing “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads” ([[Rev.7.3|Revelation 7:3]]).
Spurgeon’s word, common among Protestants of his day, for Roman Catholicism.
Unbelief, rejecting the Christian faith (not unfaithfulness in marriage).
Punishment, discipline.

notes.term: “Thou shalt be gathered into thy grave in peace…”
notes.note: God’s promise to Josiah ([[2Kgs.22.20|2 Kings 22:20]]).

notes.term: The days of our mourning shall be ended

modern: We don’t need to work out what the hornets were. They were God’s own army, which he sent ahead of his people to sting their enemies and make Israel’s conquest easy. Our God will fight for his people by means of his own choosing, and harass their enemies before they ever come into the actual battle. He often confuses the enemies of truth by methods the reformers themselves have no hand in. The air is full of mysterious influences that trouble Israel’s enemies. We read in Revelation that “the earth helped the woman.”

Let’s never be afraid. The stars in their courses fight against the enemies of our souls. Often, when we march to the battle, we find no army to fight. “The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.” God’s hornets can do more than our weapons. We could never dream of the victory being won by the means the Lord will use. We must obey our marching orders and go out to win the nations for Jesus, and we’ll find that the Lord has gone ahead of us and prepared the way, so that in the end we’ll joyfully confess, “His own right hand, and his holy arm, have gotten him the victory.”

notes.note: God promised to send hornets ahead of Israel to drive out the peoples of Canaan, and later reminded them he had done it ([[Josh.24.12|Joshua 24:12]]).
Harass, wear down.
The book of Revelation.
The earth swallowed the flood the dragon poured out after her ([[Rev.12.16|Revelation 12:16]]).
“They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera” ([[Judg.5.20|Judges 5:20]]).
An army.
Moses’ words at the Red Sea ([[Exod.14.14|Exodus 14:14]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: Our God can’t forget his servants in the sense of ceasing to love them. He chose them not for a time, but forever. He knew what they would be when he called them into the divine family. He blots out their sins like a cloud, and we can be sure he won’t turn them out of doors for sins he has blotted out. It would be blasphemy to imagine such a thing.

He won’t forget them in the sense of ceasing to think of them. One forgetful moment on our God’s part would ruin us. So he says, “Thou shalt not be forgotten of me.” People forget us. Those we’ve helped turn against us. We have no lasting place in people’s fickle hearts. But God will never forget one of his true servants. He binds himself to us not by what we do for him, but by what he has done for us. We’ve been loved too long and bought at too great a price to be forgotten now. Jesus sees in us the fruit of his soul’s anguish, and he can never forget that. The Father sees in us his Son’s bride, and the Spirit sees in us his own effective work. The Lord thinks about us. Today we’ll be helped and held up. Oh, that we may never forget the Lord!

notes.note: The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: He blots out their sins like a cloud
notes.note: “I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions” ([[Isa.44.22|Isaiah 44:22]]), the verse after the day’s text.

notes.term: Bought at too great a price
notes.note: “Ye are bought with a price” ([[1Cor.6.20|1 Corinthians 6:20]]).
The anguish of his suffering. “He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied” ([[Isa.53.11|Isaiah 53:11]]).
Bride; here, the church.
Effective; actually doing what it sets out to do.
“I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me” ([[Ps.40.17|Psalm 40:17]]).
Helped and relieved.

modern: What a blessed prospect! This is no dream of a fanatic, but the statement of the Word that cannot err. The Lord will be known among all peoples, and every tribe of humanity will acknowledge his gracious rule. Today it’s far from being so. Where do any bow before the great King? How much rebellion there is! How many lords and how many gods there are on the earth! Even among those who call themselves Christians, what different ideas there are about him and his gospel! One day there will be one King, one Lord, and one name for the living God. O Lord, hurry that day! We cry every day, “Thy kingdom come.”

We won’t argue about when this will be, in case we lose the comfort of the certainty that it will be. As surely as the Holy Spirit spoke by his prophets, so surely will the whole earth be filled with the glory of the Lord. Jesus didn’t die in vain. The Spirit of God doesn’t work in vain. The Father’s eternal purposes won’t be frustrated. Here, where Satan triumphed, Jesus will be crowned, and the Lord God Almighty will reign. Let’s go to our daily work and warfare, made strong in faith.

notes.note: In Spurgeon’s day, a religious fanatic with wild private visions.
Unable to be wrong.
[[1Cor.8.5|1 Corinthians 8:5]].
From the Lord’s Prayer ([[Matt.6.10|Matthew 6:10]]).

notes.term: The whole earth… filled with the glory of the Lord
notes.note: “The earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea” ([[Hab.2.14|Habakkuk 2:14]]).

notes.term: The Lord God Omnipotent shall reign
notes.note: “Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth” ([[Rev.19.6|Revelation 19:6]]). Omnipotent means all-powerful.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: Then we have no reason to be afraid of them. That would show a cowardly spirit, and be a sign of unbelief rather than faith. God can make us so like himself that people will be forced to see that we rightly bear his name and truly belong to the holy Lord. Oh, that we may receive this grace, which the Lord is waiting to give!

You can be sure that ungodly people are afraid of true saints. They hate them, but they also fear them. Haman trembled because of Mordecai, even while he was plotting the good man’s destruction. In fact, their hatred often comes from a dread they’re too proud to admit. Let’s follow the path of truth and uprightness without the slightest tremor. Fear isn’t for us, but for those who do wrong and fight against the Lord of hosts. If the name of the eternal God really is named on us, we’re safe. In the old days a Roman only had to say *Romanus sum*, “I am a Roman,” and he could claim the protection of all the legions of that vast empire. In the same way, everyone who is a man of God has almighty power as his guardian, and God would sooner empty heaven of angels than leave a saint without defense. Be braver than lions for the right, for God is with you.

notes.note: Low, poor-spirited (not unkind).
Haman, the Persian king’s chief minister, plotted to destroy Mordecai and all the Jews, but his own wife warned him, “thou shalt not prevail against him” ([[Esth.6.13|Esther 6:13]]).
God as commander of the armies of heaven.
Latin for “I am a Roman.” Paul’s Roman citizenship saved him from a flogging ([[Acts.22.25-Acts.22.29|Acts 22:25–29]]).
Being all-powerful.
“The righteous are bold as a lion” ([[Prov.28.1|Proverbs 28:1]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: Are you a witness for the Lord, and are you in danger right now? Then remember that you are immortal until your work is done. If the Lord has more witnessing for you to do, you’ll live to do it. Who can break the vessel the Lord means to use again?

If there’s no more work for you to do for your Master, it can’t distress you that he’s about to take you home and put you where you’ll be beyond the reach of your enemies. Bearing witness for Jesus is your chief concern, and you can’t be stopped from it until it’s finished, so be at peace. Cruel slander, wicked misrepresentation, desertion by friends, betrayal by the one you trusted most, and whatever else may come can’t hinder the Lord’s purpose for you. The Lord stands by you in the night of your sorrow and says, “Thou must yet bear witness for me.” Be calm; be filled with joy in the Lord.

If you don’t need this promise right now, you may very soon. Store it up. Remember also to pray for missionaries and for everyone who is persecuted, that the Lord will keep them safe until their life’s work is complete.

notes.note: The night after the riot in Jerusalem, with Paul held in the Roman fort and forty men sworn to kill him ([[Acts.23.10-Acts.23.12|Acts 23:10–12]]).

notes.term: Immortal till your work is done
notes.note: A well-known saying among Christians of Spurgeon’s day.

notes.term: The vessel which the Lord intends again to use
notes.note: “A vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use” ([[2Tim.2.21|2 Timothy 2:21]]).
Enemies.

modern: Yes, a true love for the great Book will bring us great peace from the great God, and be a great protection to us. Let’s live constantly in the company of the law of the Lord, and it will grow in our hearts a restfulness nothing else can. The Holy Spirit acts as a Comforter through the Word, and pours out those gentle influences that calm the storms of the soul.

Nothing trips up the person who has the Word of God living in him richly. He takes up his daily cross, and it becomes a delight. He’s ready for the fiery trial and doesn’t think it strange, so it doesn’t throw him into utter despair. He isn’t tripped up by prosperity, as so many are, or crushed by hardship, as others have been, because he lives above the changing circumstances of outward life. When his Lord sets before him some great mystery of the faith that makes others cry, “This is an hard saying; who can hear it?” the believer accepts it without question, because his intellectual difficulties are overcome by his reverent awe of the law of the Lord, which is to him the supreme authority, and he joyfully bows to it. Lord, work this love, this peace, this rest in us today.

notes.note: Nothing will make them stumble.
Company.
The Holy Spirit; Jesus’ name for him in John 14:26.
Pours out ([[Rom.5.5|Romans 5:5]]).
Kindly, gentle.
“Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom” ([[Col.3.16|Colossians 3:16]]).
“Think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you” ([[1Pet.4.12|1 Peter 4:12]]).
What many disciples said when Jesus called himself the bread of life, before they turned back ([[John.6.60|John 6:60]]).

modern: This is a glorious picture of the gospel. Jesus, numbered with the transgressors, hangs before us on the cross. A look to him will heal us of the serpent’s bite of sin, and heal us at once: “When he looketh upon it, he shall live.” Let the reader who is grieving over their sinfulness notice the words: “Everyone that looketh upon it shall live.” Everyone who looks will find this true. I’ve found it so. I looked to Jesus and lived at once. I know I did. Reader, if you look to Jesus, you’ll live too. True, you’re swelling with the venom, and you see no hope. True, also, there is no hope but this one. But this is no doubtful cure: “Everyone that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.”

The bronze serpent wasn’t lifted up as a curiosity for healthy people to stare at. Its special purpose was for those who had been “bitten.” Jesus died as a real Savior for real sinners. Whether the bite has made you a drunkard, or a thief, or impure, or profane, a look at the great Savior will heal you of these diseases and make you live in holiness and fellowship with God. Look and live.

notes.note: When poisonous snakes bit the Israelites in the wilderness, God had Moses make a bronze snake and set it on a pole ([[Num.21.6-Num.21.9|Numbers 21:6–9]]). Jesus compared it to his own lifting up on the cross ([[John.3.14-John.3.15|John 3:14–15]]).
A person or event in the Old Testament that pictures Christ ahead of time.

notes.term: I looked to Jesus and lived
notes.note: Spurgeon was converted at fifteen, hearing a sermon on “Look unto me, and be ye saved” ([[Isa.45.22|Isaiah 45:22]]).
Made of brass or bronze.
Irreverent; treating holy things with contempt.

modern: Truly, whatever else we don’t know, we know the Lord. This promise is true in our experience today, and it’s no small one. The least believer among us knows God in Christ Jesus. Not as fully as we’d like, but still truly and really, we know the Lord. We don’t only know doctrines about him; we know *him*. He’s our Father and our Friend. We know him personally. We can say, “My Lord, and my God.” We’re on terms of close fellowship with God, and we spend many a happy time in his holy company. We’re no longer strangers to our God; the secret of the Lord is with us.

This is more than nature could have taught us. Flesh and blood hasn’t revealed God to us. Christ Jesus has made the Father known to our hearts. So if the Lord has made us know him, isn’t this the fountain of all saving knowledge? To know God is eternal life. As soon as we come to know God, we have the evidence that we’ve been made alive into newness of life. O my soul, rejoice in this knowledge, and bless your God all day today!

notes.note: Part of God’s promise of a new covenant ([[Jer.31.31-Jer.31.34|Jeremiah 31:31–34]]).
Thomas’s words to the risen Jesus ([[John.20.28|John 20:28]]).
“The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him” ([[Ps.25.14|Psalm 25:14]]).

notes.term: Flesh and blood has not revealed
notes.note: Jesus’ words to Peter ([[Matt.16.17|Matthew 16:17]]).

notes.term: To know God is eternal life
notes.note: “This is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God” ([[John.17.3|John 17:3]]).
Made alive into a new life ([[Rom.6.4|Romans 6:4]]).

modern: When we know the Lord, we receive forgiveness of sins. We know him as the God of grace, who passes over our wrongdoing. What a joyful discovery this is!

But how divinely this promise is worded: the Lord promises to remember our sins no more! Can God forget? He says he will, and he means what he says. He’ll treat us as though we had never sinned. The great atonement removed all sin so completely that to the mind of God it no longer exists. The believer in Christ Jesus is now as accepted as Adam in his innocence; no, more so, for he wears a divine righteousness, while Adam’s was only human.

The great Lord won’t remember our sins in order to punish them, or to love us one bit less because of them. As a debt stops being a debt when it’s paid, so the Lord wipes out the sin of his people completely.

When we’re grieving over our sins and failures, as it’s our duty to do as long as we live, let’s at the same time rejoice that they’ll never be brought up against us. This makes us hate sin. God’s free pardon makes us eager never again to grieve him by disobedience.

notes.note: Sin, wickedness.
“Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression” ([[Mic.7.18|Micah 7:18]]).
Making peace between God and sinners by paying for sin.
Effectively, completely.
Wiping out completely.

notes.term: I will remember their sin no more
notes.note: Quoted twice in [[Heb.8.12|Hebrews 8:12]] and [[Heb.10.17|10:17]].

modern: Often when we’re racked with pain and can’t think or worship, we feel that this really is “the body of our humiliation.” And when we’re tempted by the passions that rise from the flesh, we don’t think the word “vile” at all too strong a translation. Our bodies humble us, and that’s about the best thing they do for us. Oh, that we were as lowly as we should be, since our bodies link us with the animals, and even with the dust!

But our Savior, the Lord Jesus, will change all this. We’ll be shaped like his own body of glory. This will happen in everyone who believes in Jesus. By faith their souls have been transformed, and their bodies will go through a renewal that fits them for their reborn spirits. We can’t tell how soon this grand transformation will happen, but the thought of it should help us bear today’s trials and all the troubles of the flesh. In a little while we’ll be as Jesus is now. No more aching foreheads, no more swollen limbs, no more dim eyes, no more fainting hearts. The old man will no longer be a bundle of weaknesses, nor the sick man a mass of agony. “Like unto his glorious body.” What an expression! Even our flesh will rest in hope of such a resurrection!

notes.note: Here, lowly and humble rather than wicked.
A closer translation of the Greek in [[Phil.3.21|Philippians 3:21]], used in the Revised Version of 1881.
Shaped.
Born again.
Weaknesses.
“My flesh also shall rest in hope” ([[Ps.16.9|Psalm 16:9]]).

modern: Our enemies would hand us a very dreary share, but we aren’t left in their hands. The Lord will make us stand in our lot, and our place is appointed by his infinite wisdom. A wiser mind than our own arranges our destiny. The ordering of all things is with God, and we’re glad it is; we choose that God should choose for us. If we could have our own way, we’d want to let everything go God’s way.

Knowing our own foolishness, we wouldn’t want to rule our own destinies. We feel safer and more at ease when the Lord steers our ship than we possibly could if we steered it by our own judgment. Joyfully we leave the painful present and the unknown future with our Father, our Savior, our Comforter.

O my soul, lay down your wishes at Jesus’ feet today! If you’ve lately been rather wayward and willful, eager to be and to do as you please, now dismiss your foolish self and put the reins in the Lord’s hands. Say, “He shall choose.” If others dispute the Lord’s sovereignty and boast in man’s free will, answer them, “He shall choose for me.” It’s my freest choice to let him choose. As a free agent, I choose that he should have complete control.

notes.note: The psalm goes on, “the excellency of Jacob whom he loved” ([[Ps.47.4|Psalm 47:4]]).

notes.term: Allot us a very dreary portion
notes.note: Hand out a gloomy share to us.
Stand in our appointed place. “Thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days” ([[Dan.12.13|Daniel 12:13]]).
Appointing, deciding.
God’s right and power to rule and to choose freely, answering to no one.
Someone who acts by their own free choice.
I choose.

modern: Because it’s a righteous desire, it’s safe for God to grant it. It would be good neither for the person himself nor for society at large for such a promise to be made to the unrighteous. Let’s keep the Lord’s commands, and he will rightly pay attention to our desires.

When righteous people are left to desire unrighteous things, those desires won’t be granted. But then these aren’t their real desires; they’re their wanderings or blunders, and it’s good that they should be refused. Their gracious desires will come before the Lord, and he won’t say no to them.

Does the Lord refuse our requests for a while? Let today’s promise encourage us to ask again. Has he refused us altogether? We’ll still thank him, because it was always our desire that he should refuse us if he judged a refusal best.

There are some things we ask for very boldly. Our chief desires are for holiness, usefulness, likeness to Christ and readiness for heaven. These are the desires of grace rather than of nature, the desires of the righteous man rather than of the mere man. God won’t be stingy with us in these things, but will do for us exceeding abundantly. “Delight thyself also in the Lord, and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.” Today, my soul, ask big!

notes.term: The desire of the righteous shall be granted
notes.note: The verse begins, “The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him” ([[Prov.10.24|Proverbs 10:24]]).
Pay attention to, look kindly on.
Refuse them.
Give too little; hold back.
“Him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think” ([[Eph.3.20|Ephesians 3:20]]).

modern: What a happy day it will be when everything is set apart for God, and even the horses’ bells ring out holiness to the Lord! That day has come for me. Don’t I make everything holy to God? These clothes, as I put them on or take them off, shouldn’t they remind me of the righteousness of Christ Jesus my Lord? Shouldn’t my work be done as for the Lord? Oh, that today my clothes may be priestly robes, my meals sacraments, my house a temple, my table an altar, my speech incense and myself a priest! Lord, keep your promise, and let nothing be common or unclean to me.

Let me expect this in faith. Believing it is so, I’ll be helped to make it so. Since I myself belong to Jesus, my Lord may take an inventory of everything I have, because it’s all his own; and I’m determined to prove it by the use I put it to today. From morning till evening I want to order everything by a happy and holy rule. My bells will ring; why shouldn’t they? Even my horses will have bells; who has a better right to music than the saints? But all my bells, my music, my mirth will be turned to holiness, and will ring out the name of “The Happy God.”

notes.note: The words engraved on the high priest’s gold plate ([[Exod.28.36|Exodus 28:36]]). Zechariah foresees them on ordinary horse bells and cooking pots ([[Zech.14.20-Zech.14.21|Zechariah 14:20–21]]).
Set apart for God.
Robes worn by priests in worship.
Holy acts of worship, such as the Lord’s Supper.
Peter’s words in his vision ([[Acts.10.14|Acts 10:14]]).
“Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord” ([[Col.3.23|Colossians 3:23]]).
Paul speaks of “the blessed God” ([[1Tim.1.11|1 Timothy 1:11]]), where the Greek word can mean “happy.”

modern: I must make sure my ways please the Lord. Even then I’ll have enemies, and perhaps all the more surely because I’m trying to do what is right. But what a promise this is! The Lord will make the wrath of man praise him, and hold it back so that it won’t distress me.

He can make an enemy stop harming me, even though he’d like to. He did this with Laban, who chased Jacob but didn’t dare touch him. Or he can calm the enemy’s anger and make him friendly, as he did with Esau, who met Jacob like a brother, though Jacob had dreaded that he would strike down him and his family with the sword. The Lord can also turn a furious enemy into a brother in Christ and a fellow worker, as he did with Saul of Tarsus. Oh, that he would do this wherever a persecuting spirit shows itself!

Happy is the person whose enemies are made to be to him what the lions were to Daniel in the den: quiet and good company! When I meet death, who is called the last enemy, I pray that I may be at peace. Only let my great concern be to please the Lord in everything. Oh, for faith and holiness, for these are a pleasure to the Most High!

notes.term: The wrath of man to praise Him
notes.note: “Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: the remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain” ([[Ps.76.10|Psalm 76:10]]).
Lessen, hold back.
Stop.
God warned Laban in a dream not to harm Jacob as he chased him ([[Gen.31.24|Genesis 31:24]]).
Esau ran to meet Jacob, embraced him and kissed him ([[Gen.33.4|Genesis 33:4]]).
The persecutor who became the apostle Paul ([[Acts.9.1-Acts.9.6|Acts 9:1–6]]).
“My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths” ([[Dan.6.22|Daniel 6:22]]).
“The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death” ([[1Cor.15.26|1 Corinthians 15:26]]).

modern: This word to Joshua is often quoted; it’s the basis of that New Testament word, “He hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.”

Dear friend, a life of warfare lies ahead of us, but the Lord of hosts is with us. Are we called to lead a great but fickle people? This promise guarantees us all the wisdom and good sense we’ll need. Do we have to fight cunning and powerful enemies? Here is strength and courage, skill and victory. Do we have a vast inheritance to win? By this sign we’ll achieve our goal: the Lord himself is with us.

It really would be terrible for us if the Lord could fail us; but since that can never happen, the winds of worry are laid to sleep in the caves of God’s faithfulness. Not on a single occasion will the Lord desert us. Whatever happens, he’ll be at our side. Friends drop away from us; their help is only an April shower. But God is faithful, Jesus is the same forever, and the Holy Spirit lives in us.

Come, my heart, be calm and hopeful today. Clouds may gather, but the Lord can blow them away. Since God won’t fail me, my faith won’t fail; and as he won’t forsake me, I won’t forsake him. Oh, for a restful faith!

notes.note: God’s promise as Joshua took over from Moses ([[Josh.1.5|Joshua 1:5]]).

notes.term: “He hath said, I will never leave thee…”
notes.note: [[Heb.13.5|Hebrews 13:5]].
God as commander of the armies of heaven.

notes.term: Jesus is the same for ever
notes.note: “Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever” ([[Heb.13.8|Hebrews 13:8]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: He does this at the very start, when his chosen ones are like wandering sheep that don’t know the Shepherd or the fold. How wonderfully the Lord finds his chosen! Jesus is great as a seeking Shepherd as well as a saving Shepherd. Though many of those his Father gave him have gone as near to the gate of hell as they could, the Lord, by searching and seeking, finds them and comes near to them in grace. He sought us out; let’s have good hope for those we carry on our hearts in prayer, for he’ll find them too.

The Lord does the same again when any of his flock stray from the pastures of truth and holiness. They may fall into serious error, sad sin and grievous hardness of heart; but the Lord, who has become a guarantor for them to his Father, won’t let one of them go so far as to perish. By providence and grace he’ll follow them into foreign lands, into homes of poverty, into hiding places of obscurity, into the depths of despair. He won’t lose one of all the Father has given him. It’s a point of honor with Jesus to seek and save the whole flock, without a single exception. What a promise to plead, if right now I’m forced to cry, “I have gone astray like a lost sheep”!

notes.term: I will both search my sheep
notes.note: The text is [[Ezek.34.11|Ezekiel 34:11]] (the heading’s “Exodus” is a misprint), part of God’s promise to shepherd his scattered flock himself.
God’s chosen people.
The gate of hell.
A guarantor: someone who promises to pay another’s debt.
Allow.
God’s care and control over everything that happens, providing for his people.
“Of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing” ([[John.6.39|John 6:39]]).
“The Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost” ([[Luke.19.10|Luke 19:10]]).

notes.term: “I have gone astray like a lost sheep”

modern: I won’t die. I can and do believe in the Lord my God, and this faith will keep me alive. I want to be counted among those who are just in their lives; but even if I were perfect, I wouldn’t try to live by my own righteousness. I’d cling to the work of the Lord Jesus, and still live by faith in him and by nothing else. If I were able to give my body to be burned for my Lord Jesus, I still wouldn’t trust in my own courage and steadfastness, but would still live by faith.

Living by faith is a far surer and happier thing than living by feelings or by works. The branch, by living in the vine, lives a better life than it would live by itself, even if it could live at all apart from the stem. To live by clinging to Jesus, drawing everything from him, is a sweet and sacred thing. If even the most just must live like this, how much more must I, a poor sinner! Lord, I believe. I must trust you completely. What else can I do? Trusting you is my life. I feel it to be so. I’ll hold to this right to the end.

notes.term: The just shall live by faith
notes.note: Paul quotes [[Hab.2.4|Habakkuk 2:4]] in [[Rom.1.17|Romans 1:17]]. “The just” are those made right with God.

notes.term: Give my body to be burned
notes.note: [[1Cor.13.3|1 Corinthians 13:3]].
Steadfastness, faithfulness.
Beg, plead.
“As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me” ([[John.15.4|John 15:4]]).
Hold to, stand by.

modern: We’re to give to the poor out of pity. Not to be seen and applauded, still less to gain influence over them, but out of pure sympathy and compassion we must help them.

We mustn’t expect to get anything back from the poor, not even gratitude, but we should see what we’ve done as a loan to the Lord. He takes on the debt, and if we look to him in the matter, we mustn’t look to the second party. What an honor the Lord gives us when he stoops to borrow from us! The merchant who has the Lord on his books is greatly favored. It would seem a pity to have such a name down for a measly sum; let’s make it a large amount. The next needy person who comes our way, let’s help him.

As for repayment, we can hardly think of it, and yet here is the Lord’s written promise to pay. Blessed be his name, his promise to pay is better than gold and silver. Are we running a little short because of the hard times? We may humbly venture to present this bill at the Bank of Faith. Has any of our readers been a bit of a miser toward the poor? Poor soul. May the Lord forgive him.

notes.note: [[Prov.19.17|Proverbs 19:17]].
Stoops down kindly from a high position.
A tiny, miserable sum.
A signed written promise to pay.
The long trade slump of the 1880s, when Spurgeon wrote this book.
A play on *The Bank of Faith*, a well-known book by the preacher William Huntington about God answering his prayers for money and food.
Old slang for a miser.

modern: Am I bowed down? Then let me press this word of grace before the Lord. It’s his way, his custom, his promise, his delight to raise up those who are bowed down. Is it a sense of sin, and the low spirits that come with it, that’s troubling me now? Then the work of Jesus is made and provided for exactly this case, to raise me up into rest. O Lord, raise me, for your mercy’s sake!

Is it a sad bereavement or a great fall in circumstances? Here again the Comforter has taken on the work of consoling. What a mercy for us that one person of the holy Trinity should become the Comforter! This work will be done well, since so glorious a One has made it his special care.

Some are so bowed down that only Jesus can free them from their weakness, but he can and he will. He can raise us up to health, to hope, to happiness. He has often done it in earlier trials, and he is the same Savior and will repeat his acts of loving-kindness. We who are bowed down and sorrowful today will yet be set on high, and those who mock us now will be greatly ashamed. What an honor to be raised up by the Lord! It’s worth being bowed down to experience his raising power.

notes.term: The Lord raiseth them that are bowed down

notes.note: Press, plead.
The death of someone close.
The Holy Spirit; Jesus’ name for him in John 14:26.
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd).
Jesus freed a woman bent double for eighteen years: “Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity” ([[Luke.13.11-Luke.13.13|Luke 13:11–13]]).

modern: We must go through the first death, unless the Lord suddenly comes to his temple. Let’s live ready for it, waiting for it without fear, since Jesus has turned death from a dreary cave into a passage that leads to glory.

The thing to fear isn’t the first death but the second; not the parting of the soul from the body, but the final separation of the whole person from God. This is death indeed. This death kills all peace, joy, happiness and hope. When God is gone, everything is gone. A death like this is far worse than ceasing to exist: it’s existence without the life that makes existence worth having.

Now, if by God’s grace we fight on to the end and conquer in the glorious war, no second death can lay its cold finger on us. We’ll have no fear of death and hell, for we’ll receive a crown of life that never fades. How this strengthens us for the fight! Eternal life is worth a lifetime’s battle. To escape the harm of the second death is worth struggling for all our lives.
Lord, give us faith so that we may overcome, and then give us grace to stay unharmed though sin and Satan dog our heels!

notes.note: The final judgment, “the lake of fire. This is the second death” ([[Rev.20.14|Revelation 20:14]]).
“The Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple” ([[Mal.3.1|Malachi 3:1]]).
Remain, stay.

notes.term: A crown of life which fadeth not away
notes.note: “Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life” ([[Rev.2.10|Revelation 2:10]]); “a crown of glory that fadeth not away” ([[1Pet.5.4|1 Peter 5:4]]).
Gives us courage and strength.
Follow close behind us.

modern: Many read and plead this promise without noticing the condition on which the blessing is promised. We can’t expect heaven to be opened or blessing poured out unless we pay what we owe to the Lord our God and to his cause. There’d be no lack of funds for holy purposes if all professing Christians paid their fair share.

Many are poor because they rob God. Many churches, too, miss out on the visits of the Spirit because they starve their ministers. If there’s no earthly food for God’s servants, we needn’t be surprised if their ministry has little food in it for our souls. When missions are pining for funds, and the work of the Lord is held back by an empty treasury, how can we expect much prosperity of soul?

Come, come! What have I given lately? Have I been stingy with my God? Have I held back from my Savior? This will never do. Let me give my Lord Jesus his tithe by helping the poor and supporting his work, and then I’ll prove his power to bless me on a large scale.

notes.note: A tenth of one’s income, given to God.
Food of any kind.
Put me to the test.
“Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me… In tithes and offerings” ([[Mal.3.8|Malachi 3:8]]).
Publicly claiming to be a Christian. A “dead profession” is the claim with no faith behind it.
Belonging to this passing life.
Stingy, ungenerous.
Given too little to; held back from.

modern: Worry about our family is natural, but we’ll be wise if we turn it into care about our own character. If we walk before the Lord in integrity, we’ll do more to bless our descendants than if we left them large estates. A father’s holy life is a rich inheritance for his sons.
The upright man leaves his heirs his example, and that in itself will be a mine of true wealth. How many people can trace their success in life to the example of their parents!

He also leaves them his good name. People think all the better of us as the sons of a man who could be trusted, the successors of a tradesman with an excellent reputation. Oh, that all young men were eager to keep up the family name!

Above all, he leaves his children his prayers and the blessing of a God who hears prayer, and these make our children favored among the sons of men. God will save them even after we’re dead. Oh, that they might be saved right away!

Our integrity may be God’s means of saving our sons and daughters. If they see the truth of our faith proved by our lives, it may be that they’ll believe in Jesus for themselves. Lord, fulfill this word for my household!

notes.term: The just man walketh in his integrity
notes.note: [[Prov.20.7|Proverbs 20:7]].
Left to someone in a will.
Something handed down to those who come after.
Reputation, good name.
A shopkeeper or craftsman.
Like the promise to the jailer at Philippi: “Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house” ([[Acts.16.31|Acts 16:31]]).

modern: An Israelite master was to give his bondservant freedom in due time, and when the servant left, he was to set him up in life with a generous share. This was to be done heartily and cheerfully, and then the Lord promised to bless the generous act. The spirit of this command, and indeed the whole law of Christ, binds us to treat working people well. We ought to remember how the Lord has dealt with us, and that this makes it absolutely necessary for us to deal graciously with others. It’s fitting for the children of a gracious God to be generous. How can we expect our great Master to bless us in our business if we oppress those who serve us?

What a blessing is set before the generous mind here! To be blessed in all that we do is to be blessed indeed. The Lord will send us this partly in prosperity, partly in contentment of mind and partly in a sense of his favor, which is the best of all blessings. He can make us feel that we’re under his special care and surrounded by his particular love. This makes this earthly life a joyful prelude to the life to come. God’s blessing is more than a fortune. It makes rich, and adds no sorrow with it.

notes.note: A Hebrew servant was to go free in the seventh year, and his master was to send him off well supplied from his flock, threshing floor and winepress ([[Deut.15.12-Deut.15.14|Deuteronomy 15:12–14]]).
A servant bound to work for a set time.
Generous.
A command.
“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ” ([[Gal.6.2|Galatians 6:2]]).
A blessing.
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd).

notes.term: It maketh rich, and addeth no sorrow
notes.note: “The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it” ([[Prov.10.22|Proverbs 10:22]]).

modern: The One who began it will carry on the work being done in my soul. The Lord is concerned about everything that concerns me. Everything that is good now, but not yet perfect, the Lord will watch over, protect and carry through to completion. This is a great comfort. I couldn’t perfect the work of grace myself. I’m quite sure of that, because I fail every day, and I’ve only held on this long because the Lord has helped me. If the Lord left me, all my past experience would count for nothing, and I’d perish on the way. But the Lord will keep blessing me. He’ll perfect my faith, my love, my character, my life’s work. He’ll do this because he has begun a work in me. He gave me the concern I feel, and in some measure he has fulfilled my gracious longings. He never leaves a work unfinished; that wouldn’t be for his glory, and it wouldn’t be like him. He knows how to carry out his gracious plan, and though my own evil nature, the world and the devil all plot to hinder him, I don’t doubt his promise. He will perfect what concerns me, and I’ll praise him forever. Lord, let your gracious work make some progress today!

notes.term: The Lord will perfect that which concerneth me
notes.note: [[Ps.138.8|Psalm 138:8]]. To perfect is to bring to completion.
“He which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ” ([[Phil.1.6|Philippians 1:6]]).
Worked.
Longings, hopes.
Plot together.

modern: Here is a shared belonging. Each belongs to the other. God is his people’s portion, and the chosen people are their God’s portion. The saints find in God their chief possession, and he counts them his special treasure. What a mine of comfort there is in this for every believer!

This happy state of belonging to each other leads to thinking of each other. God will always think of his own people, and they will always think of him. Today my God will do everything for me; what can I do for him? My thoughts ought to run toward him, since he thinks about me. Let me make sure that they do, and not be content with merely admitting that they ought to.
This leads, again, to fellowship with each other. God lives in us, and we live in him. He walks with us, and we walk with God. What happy fellowship!

Oh, for grace to treat the Lord as my God: to trust him and to serve him as his Godhead deserves! Oh, that I could love, worship, adore and obey the Lord in spirit and in truth! This is my heart’s desire. When I reach it, I’ll have found my heaven. Lord, help me! Be my God in helping me know you as my God, for Jesus’ sake.

notes.note: Paul quotes God’s promise from [[Lev.26.12|Leviticus 26:12]] in [[2Cor.6.16|2 Corinthians 6:16]].
A share, a stake.
A share of an inheritance. When God is “our portion”, he himself is what we inherit, and he is enough.
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd). “Ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me” ([[Exod.19.5|Exodus 19:5]]).
Close fellowship and sharing, with God or with each other. (Also the Lord’s Supper.)
God’s divine nature; his being God.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: Don’t be in a hurry. Let your anger cool down. Say nothing and do nothing to get revenge. You’ll be sure to act unwisely if you take up the fight and battle for yourself, and you certainly won’t show the spirit of the Lord Jesus. It’s nobler to forgive and let the offense go. Letting an injury fester in your heart, and brooding over revenge, keeps old wounds open and makes new ones. Better to forget and forgive.

Perhaps you say you must do something or lose a great deal. Then do what this morning’s promise advises: “Wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.” This advice won’t cost you money, but it’s worth far more. Be calm and quiet. Wait on the Lord. Tell him your grievance. Spread Rabshakeh’s letter before the Lord, and that in itself will ease your burdened mind. Besides, there’s the promise: “He shall save thee.” God will find a way to rescue you. Neither you nor I can guess how he’ll do it, but he will. If the Lord saves you, that will be a great deal better than getting into petty quarrels and covering yourself with dirt by wrestling with the unclean. Don’t be angry anymore. Leave your case with the Judge of all.

notes.note: Pay back.
Join the fight. A cudgel is a heavy club.
Fester; go on hurting.
Perhaps.

The Assyrian commander Rabshakeh mocked Jerusalem and its God. When the threatening letter followed, King Hezekiah took it into the temple “and spread it before the LORD” ([[Isa.37.14|Isaiah 37:14]]).
A case brought to a judge.
“Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” ([[Gen.18.25|Genesis 18:25]]).

modern: My heart, be stirred up to keep going in the holy war, for the reward of victory is great. Today we eat heavenly food that falls around our camps: the food of the wilderness, the food that comes from heaven, the food that never fails the pilgrims to Canaan. But there is a still higher degree of spiritual life kept for us in Christ Jesus, and food for it that is still hidden from our experience. In the golden pot that was laid up in the ark, a portion of manna was hidden away, and though it was kept for ages, it never went stale. No one ever saw it; it was hidden with the ark of the covenant in the Holy of Holies. In the same way, the believer’s highest life is hidden with Christ in God. We’ll come to it soon. Made victorious through the grace of our Lord Jesus, we’ll eat the King’s food and feast on royal delicacies. We’ll feed on Jesus. He is our “hidden manna” as well as the manna of the wilderness. He is all in all to us in our highest condition as well as our lowest. He helps us fight, gives us the victory, and then is himself our reward. Lord, help me to overcome.

notes.term: The hidden manna… a white stone
notes.note: Christ’s promise to the church at Pergamos ([[Rev.2.17|Revelation 2:17]]). In ancient courts a white stone could mean “not guilty,” and it also served as a ticket to a feast.
The bread from heaven that fed Israel in the wilderness ([[Exod.16.15|Exodus 16:15]]).
A jar of manna kept before the Lord ([[Exod.16.33|Exodus 16:33]]), later in the ark ([[Heb.9.4|Hebrews 9:4]]).
The innermost room of the tabernacle and temple, where God’s presence was.
“Your life is hid with Christ in God” ([[Col.3.3|Colossians 3:3]]).
Delicacies, fine food.
Condition.
